- Completed `RH-W-0043`: a builder version bump no longer freezes the installations it exists to update. Two gates combined to cause it: replacement required the installed file to already carry the current version, which an installed file cannot do during an upgrade, and an installed checker that was not byte-equal to the current template narrowed the owned set to itself. Measuring before fixing found the trap in the obvious repair, because relaxing the version gate alone leaves the new checker naming a manifest nobody wrote and the installed checker dies with `ValueError: manifest digest mismatch`. Both halves landed together, so the checker and its manifest move in the same transaction. The security boundary was widened deliberately and stated in the issue: byte equality proves freshness, not authenticity, and cannot hold across versions, while every replacement still requires builder provenance on the file being replaced. Four contract documents that still declared the superseded current-version rule were corrected in the same unit. A pre-merge probe also confirmed that the migration and the ordinary replacement never handle the checker and manifest twice, and found an unpredicted gain: a prior-era legacy migration now regenerates its six command wrappers in the same pass, closing the dangling-command window the `v3.1-rc.4` consumer run exposed.
